name: Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT)
summary: An attention-based deep model for multi-horizon forecasting with quantile outputs and built-in interpretability.
inputs: A panel of related series with static covariates, known-future inputs and observed inputs.
outputs: Quantile forecasts over several horizons; variable-importance and attention weights.

data_requirements.min_observations: Many series or long histories; small data overfits

assumptions: Many related series (a panel) with static, known-future and observed inputs
Enough data to train an attention model
math_summary: Combines recurrent layers for local processing with interpretable multi-head self-attention for long-range dependencies, gating and variable-selection networks, and outputs quantiles via a quantile loss.
when_to_use: Panels of related series with known future inputs (calendars, schedules)
When you need quantile forecasts and some interpretability (variable importance, attention)
when_not_to_use: Tight compute budgets; tree models with lag features are cheaper strong baselines
pitfalls: Attention weights are not causal explanations

compute.complexity: O(T^2) attention over the lookback window plus recurrent layers.
compute.hardware: GPU recommended for training at scale; small configs on CPU are slow but possible.

applicability.use_case: Day-ahead electricity load and price quantiles across regions
Multi-horizon realised-volatility forecasting (the paper includes a volatility dataset)
